core_obligations: Reduce to stalks (proof lines 10992-10994): it suffices to show that the stalk of R^q j_*G_{m,eta} vanishes at every geometric point of X for q at least one.

Case of a closed point (proof lines 10997-11018): for a geometric point over a closed point x the author identifies the stalk with the cohomology of G_m over the fraction field of the strict henselization, which is a field of transcendence degree one over k, and applies the vanishing result for such fields.

Case of the generic point (proof lines 11020-11032): for the geometric point over the generic point the stalk becomes the cohomology of G_m over the separable closure of the function field, which vanishes in positive degrees because the corresponding Galois group is trivial.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the statement to the vanishing of the stalks at all geometric points.
Over a closed point, identify the stalk with the cohomology of G_m over a field of transcendence degree one and apply the vanishing theorem.
Over the generic point, use that the Galois group is trivial.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the higher direct images of the multiplicative group along the inclusion of the generic point of a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field vanish (statement lines 10987-10990, with the standing set-up delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 10937-10941). The proof reduces to the vanishing of the stalks at geometric points (proof lines 10992-10994), computes the stalk over a closed point as the cohomology of the multiplicative group over the fraction field of a strict henselization, which has transcendence degree one over the base field, and applies the vanishing theorem for such fields (proof lines 10997-11018), the case of the generic point being immediate because the Galois group is trivial (proof lines 11020-11032). The non-formal content is the identification of the stalk with a cohomology group over a field of transcendence degree one. The claim is H2: one reduction plus two short case computations.
